m:
Rize Province (Turkish: Rize ili) is a province of northeast Turkey, on the eastern Black Sea coast between Trabzon and Artvin. The province of Erzurum is to the south. Its area is 3,835 km2, and its population is 344,016 (2022). The capital is the city of Rize. It was formerly known as Lazistan, however the designation of the term of Lazistan was officially banned in 1926.
The province is home to Turkish, Laz, Hemshin and Georgian communities.

Q975280:
The Kaçkar Mountains, formerly known as the Lazistan Mountains or the Mountains of Khaghtik, are a mountain range that rises above the Black Sea coast in northeastern Turkey.
With the highest peak, Kaçkar Dağı, at an elevation of 3,937 metres (12,917 ft), and mountain plateaus at about 3,000 m (9,800 ft) in elevation, the range is the highest part of the Pontic Mountains. The Kaçkars are glaciated mountains that are alpine in character, with steep rocky peaks and numerous mountain lakes. The area was declared a national park in 1994. Recreational activities in the park include hiking, camping, mountaineering, and, increasingly, heliskiing. The Kackar range boasts a wide variety of plants and wildlife such as wolves, bears, boars, feral goats, deer, jackals and wild chickens.
Q8071903:
Zilkale is a medieval castle located in the Fırtına Valley (literally "Storm Valley") within the Pontic Mountains, and is one of the most important historical structures in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize Province, within the Black Sea Region of Turkey.
The castle is built at an altitude of 1,130 m (3,710 ft), and sits at the edge of a cliff overlooking the Fırtına River (Turkish: Fırtına Deresi) approximately 380 m (1,250 ft) below, running at an elevation of 750 m (2,460 ft) southeast of it.
In the 1st-4th centuries AD it was the capital of the Laz principality of Macron-Henochi. The castle consists of the outer walls, middle walls and the inner castle. There are garrison quarters, and a possible chapel and head tower.
Q2582947: Ayder is a yayla in Rize Province, Turkey.
Q2025722: Fırtına or Peruma is one of the main water streams of Rize Province in the eastern Black Sea Region of Turkey. Its name is Turkish for "storm water". There is a group of more than 20 well-preserved Ottoman-era bridges over the Fırtına Deresi.
Q61076472: Palovit Waterfall is in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize, inside Kaçkar Mountains National Park. Fed by the Palovit stream, it falls 15 metres and is one of the highest-flow waterfalls in Rize.
Q1641126: Mount Kaçkar (Turkish: Kaçkar Dağı), with an elevation of 3,937 meters, is the highest peak in the Kaçkar Mountains. The mountain may be climbed by the northeast ridge route beginning from the village Yukarı Kavrun.
Q1025138: Hemşin, is a town in Rize Province in the Black Sea region of Turkey, 57 km from the city of Rize. It is the seat of Hemşin District. Its population is 1,472 (2021).
Q60788217: The Ardashen Church (Georgian: არდაშენის ეკლესია) or simply as Jibistasi is a Georgian Orthodox Church located in Ardeşen, Rize Province, northeastern Turkey, on the border with Georgia. The date of the church building can be traced to Middle Ages that are adjacent to the so-called late-Byzantine period. The architectural canon of the church is very well studied and it belongs to the eastern school of the mid and late Byzantine periods. According to the planning scheme, similar buildings are numerously found along the whole northern Black Sea littoral.
Q6008234:
Rize Castle (Turkish: Rize Kalesi) is a partly-ruined medieval castle located in Rize, northeastern Turkey.
Rize Castle is situated on a hill southwest of the city center, and offers a panoramic view of the city.
The castle consists of a citadel and the lower castle. It is believed that the citadel was built during the reign of Byzantine emperor Justinian I (r. 527–565), and the lower castle dates back to the 13th century.
It covers an area of 480 m2 (5,200 sq ft). The fortification's walls, built in ashlar and mortar, are 2–20 m (6.6–65.6 ft) high and 2–3 m (6.6–9.8 ft) thick. Between the cylinder-formed bastions, there are overhung support towers in various forms such as square, rectangular and round.
Today, some of the ruined castle walls are buried under reinforced concrete buildings and streets. The castle walls in the southern part were restored in 1989. The Ministry of Culture and Tourism launched a project for the restoration of Rize Castle in 2011.
Q28221174:
Rize Atatürk Museum (Turkish: Atatürk Evi Müzesi, also known as Mehmet Mataracı Konağı) is a museum in Rize, Turkey. The museum is in the Müftü quarter of Rize, and is locally known as Mehmet Mataracı mansion. It is to the east of the city stadium and to the south of the main road.
The museum building is a three-storey mansion that was built in 1921. In 1924, Mustafa Kemal Pasha (later Atatürk), the founder of the Republic of Turkey, stayed in the house during his visit to Rize. In 1981, the 100th birth year of Atatürk, the owners of the house granted it to the governorship of Rize to be used as an Atatürk museum. The museum was opened on 27 December 1985.
On the ground floor, inscriptions and tombstones are exhibited. On the first floor, there are traditional weaving instruments as well as other ethnographic items. On the second floor, memorial items of Atatürk, such as his personal belongings and photos about the Turkish War of Independence, are exhibited.
Q60289439:
Athenae or Athenai was a city and port of ancient Pontus, with a Greek temple of Athena. According to Arrian, it was 180 stadia east of the river Adienus, and 280 stadia west of Apsarus. 
According to Arrian, the place got its name from the sanctuary of Athena. Procopius, on the other hand, writes that some believe the town was named because colonists from Athens settled there. However, he states that the it actually took its name from a woman called Athenaea, who ruled the land in early times. He also adds that her tomb was still there during his time.
Arrian speaks of the place as a deserted fort, but Procopius describes it as a populous place in his time. Konrad Mannert assumes it to be the same place as the Odeinius of the Periplus of Pseudo-Scylax.
Its site is located near the modern town of Pazar, in Turkey.
Q110944940: Çat Bridge is an arch bridge in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize, 28 km from Çamlıhemşin, where the Çat and Elevit streams meet. It is 57 metres long, 15 metres high and 2.4 metres wide, and was built in 1901 by master builder Kirkor.
Q61076505: Ciha Castle is a castle in the Pazar district of Rize, 7 km from Pazar and east of the Hemşin stream. Thought to have been built by the Genoese in the 14th century for signalling and watch, it has a circular plan and an entrance flanked by two towers on the north-east.
Q21541477: Kaçkar Mountains National Park lies mostly in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize, extending into Erzurum and Artvin provinces. The 51,550-hectare park covers the Kaçkar Mountains between the Fırtına and Hemşin streams.
Q6023921: Pokut Plateau is a highland pasture at 2,032 metres south of Çamlıhemşin, Rize, between the valleys of the Fırtına and Hala streams.
Q61076450: Mikron Bridge is a 19th-century arch bridge over the Fırtına stream, 2 km from Çamlıhemşin, Rize. It is 41 metres long, 3.1 metres wide and 11 metres high; its piers were set wide apart against floods.
Q61076451: Timisvat Bridge, or Köprüköy Bridge (later renamed Osmanlı Köprüsü), is an 18th-century arch bridge over the Fırtına stream, 10 km from Ardeşen, Rize. It is 35 metres long, 2.7 metres wide and 13 metres high.
Q85968057: Apivanak Bridge is an arch bridge over the Palovit stream, a tributary of the Fırtına, in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize. It is 15 metres long, 2.5 metres wide and 2 metres above the ground, on old trade routes.
Q61076454: Şenyuva Bridge is a single-arch bridge over the Fırtına stream, 7 km from Çamlıhemşin, Rize. Built in 1696, it is 40 metres long and 20 metres high, with a pointed arch. Its inscription was lost in the 1946 flood.
Q61076441: Rize Museum, also called Rize Ethnography Museum, Tuzcuoğlu Mansion or the Yellow House, is in the Piriçelebi quarter of central Rize. It has occupied this 19th-century house, a fine example of local civil architecture, since 27 June 1998.
Q6033460: Mount Verçenik (Üçdoruk) is a 3,711-metre peak of the Kaçkar Mountains in the eastern Black Sea section of the North Anatolian Mountains. It is the second-highest summit of the Eastern Black Sea Mountains after Kaçkar and the eighth-highest mountain in Türkiye.
Q61076470: Bulut Waterfall in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize is the highest waterfall in Türkiye, dropping about 250 metres in four steps. It is fed by the Tar stream, which rises on the Altıparmak range of the Kaçkar Mountains; Seyran Tepe, where it lies, is at 2,451 metres.
Q61076474: Gelintülü Waterfall is in the Çamlıhemşin district of Rize. Fed by the Kavron stream, it falls 15 metres at an altitude of 1,320 metres.
Q61076476: Ağaran Waterfall is in the Çayeli district of Rize, 12 km from Çayeli. Fed by the Şairler stream, it takes its name ('whitening') from the white foam it throws off as it falls from a high, steep rock.
Q49175319: The Çağrankaya Highlands are three summer pastures (Aşağı Yayla, Kurtlar Yaylası and Büyük Yayla) at 2,300 metres, 9 km north-west of İkizdere, Rize. Their terrain suits off-roading, winter sports, trekking and highland tourism, and campers and nature lovers flock here in summer.
Q6033431: Anzer Plateau lies 35 km south-west of İkizdere and 54 km from Rize. It is divided into Lower Anzer (Çiçekliköy) and Upper Anzer (Ballıköy). Famous for its honey, it is also an important ecotourism area.
Q124621769: Işıklı Mosque is in the Işıklı quarter of Ardeşen, Rize. Its inscription dates it to 1887, but two Ottoman archive records show it is older.
Q61076675: The Rize Atatürk Statue is in the Piriçelebi quarter of Rize. It made the news when it was removed from the 15 July Democracy and Republic Square where it stood.
Q118947343: Güneyce Bridge is an arch bridge over the İyidere stream, 11 km from İkizdere, Rize. A lamp hangs from its arch. The arch is of cut stone and the walls of neat rubble; the parapets and deck are reinforced concrete.
Q61076466: Dereköy Bridge is a single-arch bridge with a flattened pointed arch in the İkizdere district of Rize. Its arch and parapets are of cut stone and the rest of rubble stone, with a deck of neat rubble. The parapets are square at the base and oval on top, and there are small niches inside the arch abutments, which rest on bedrock.
Q85975617: Tunca Bridge is a stone-paved arch bridge in the town of Tunca, 22 km from Ardeşen, Rize. It crosses the Tunca stream and is 28 metres long, 2.8 metres wide and 11 metres high; it is reached by a stone-stepped path south of the village.
Q109393170: Çamlıhemşin Ham Bridge, known locally as Ham Köprü, is an arch bridge just outside Çamlıhemşin, Rize, where the Hala and Çat streams meet. Its arch is of cut stone and its deck and walls of neat rubble. It was restored in 1999.
Q131402688: Tunca Bridge 2 is an arch bridge built under a large rock in the town of Tunca, 22 km from Ardeşen, Rize. It crosses the confluence of the Tunca and Selamet streams and is 20 metres long, 2.2 metres wide and 8 metres high. It once linked Tunca with the Durak valley.
Q6018846: Gito (Kito) is a highland pasture at 2,070 metres in the Çat valley of Çamlıhemşin, Rize, 31 km from the district centre.
